blocks.text: Lists par kuch operations bhi hote hain, jaise slicing (list ka ek hissa kaatna) aur concatenation (do lists jorna, + se).
Misaal: list ka ek hissa kaat kar doosri list ke saath jorein.

numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
slice = numbers [1:4]  # Gets items from index 1 to 3
extra_numbers = [6, 7]
combined = slice + extra_numbers
print(combined)
# Output : [2, 3, 4, 6, 7]

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]": paanch numbers ki list (index 0 se 4).
"slice = numbers [1:4]": slicing (hissa kaatna): index 1 se shuru, 4 se pehle ruk jata hai, yani index 1, 2, 3: [2, 3, 4].
"extra_numbers = [6, 7]": doosri list.
"combined = slice + extra_numbers": + do lists ko jor kar nayi list banata hai (concatenation): [2, 3, 4, 6, 7].
"print(combined)": nayi list print hoti hai. Aakhri line comment hai.
Output: [2, 3, 4, 6, 7]
Khud try karein: numbers [1:4] ko numbers [0:2] kar ke Run karein: [1, 2, 6, 7] aayega.
Misaal: students ke naam sort karein aur ek naam hatayein.

student_names= ["Ahmed", "Sara", "Ali", "Hina"]
student_names .sort ()
student_names . remove("Sara")
print(student_names)
# Output: ['Ahmed', 'Ali', 'Hina']

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"student_names= ["Ahmed", "Sara", "Ali", "Hina"]": chaar naamon ki list.
"student_names .sort ()": list alphabet ki tarteeb mein lagti hai: ['Ahmed', 'Ali', 'Hina', 'Sara']. Dot ke aas paas spaces ka koi asar nahi.
"student_names . remove("Sara")": "Sara" list se hat jata hai.
"print(student_names)": baqi list print hoti hai. Aakhri line comment hai.
Output: ['Ahmed', 'Ali', 'Hina']
Khud try karein: remove("Sara") ko remove("Ali") kar ke Run karein: ['Ahmed', 'Hina', 'Sara'] aayega.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab hatane wala naam "Sara " (aakhir mein space) chhapti hai. List mein "Sara" hai, "Sara " nahi, is liye remove() ValueError deta hai (x not in list). Sahi: student_names.remove("Sara"), jis ka output ['Ahmed', 'Ali', 'Hina'] hai.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text:
Farz karein aap apni pasandeeda kitabon ki list rakhte hain: ["To Kill a Mockingbird", "1984", "The Great Gatsby", "Pride and Prejudice"]. Python se yeh kaam karein:
1. Nayi kitab "Moby Dick" jorein.
2. "1984" ki jagah "Brave New World" rakhein.
3. "The Great Gatsby" hatayein.
4. Is list ko ["War and Peace", "Hamlet"] ke saath merge karein (milayein).
5. Aakhri list print karein.
In kaamon ka Python code likhein aur aakhri list print karein.

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: Lists sambhalne ke liye append() aur remove() jaise methods istemal karein. Bare projects mein data ko lists mein rakhne se code saaf aur aasan rehta hai.

blocks.prompt: Class activity: books = ["To Kill a Mockingbird", "1984", "The Great Gatsby", "Pride and Prejudice"]. "Moby Dick" jorein, "1984" ko "Brave New World" se badlein, "The Great Gatsby" hatayein, ["War and Peace", "Hamlet"] se merge karein aur print karein. Result kya hai?
blocks.explanation: books.append("Moby Dick"); books[1] = "Brave New World"; books.remove("The Great Gatsby"); books = books + ["War and Peace", "Hamlet"]; list: To Kill a Mockingbird, Brave New World, Pride and Prejudice, Moby Dick, War and Peace, Hamlet.

blocks.prompt: Do lists ko kaunsa operator jorta hai (MCQ 10)?

items: Slicing: list[start:stop] (stop shamil nahi); + se lists jurti hain.
remove() mein value bilkul wahi honi chahiye jo list mein hai.
